items.title: Black Friday, red flags: too-good-to-be-true deals hiding real threats
items.summary: How cybercriminals prepare for Black Friday: phishing, scams and malware targeting online shoppers and gamers, GTA VI- and wellness-related schemes, and fake sales spam.

items.title: The forced audit: how AuditTeam’s OpsAgent framework masks ransomware as consulting
items.summary: How does a ransomware gang sell a “forced audit”? We break down AuditTeam’s OpsAgent implant, its Rust rewrite, and the extortion model demanding a consulting fee to delete stolen data.

items.title: Operation ShadowCloud: cloud service–based backdoors targeting government networks in Asia and Africa. Part 2
items.summary: In part 2 of our analysis of the recently uncovered Operation ShadowCloud, we discuss the GraphDoor backdoor, additional plug-ins, and technical attribution.

items.title: Operation ShadowCloud: cloud service–based backdoors targeting government networks in Asia and Africa. Part 1
items.summary: In part 1 of our analysis of the recently uncovered Operation ShadowCloud, we discuss the initial infection stage, the GitDoor backdoor using GitHub as a C2, and the shellcode families it loads.

items.title: A USB worm’s second life: Retadup spreading CoffeeLoader
items.summary: A new version of CoffeeLoader is spreading through Retadup, an old USB worm whose infrastructure was seized by law enforcement back in 2019.

items.title: Ransomware at the hypervisor layer: how attackers use ESXi and vCenter features for malicious purposes
items.summary: Kaspersky experts analyze a recent ransomware incident and discuss why the hypervisor layer remains difficult to monitor, what common access paths adversaries use to reach it, and how to protect your ESXi systems.

items.title: Transcending the trust boundaries: how a cloud pentest works
items.summary: This is the first article in a series on cloud penetration testing. We'll cover the three cloud layers (External, Overlay, and Underlay), common architectures (OpenStack and Kubernetes), typical attack chains, and real-world incidents.

items.title: Citrus Ransomware: VLESS for traffic, Sn00py for encryption, and LLMs lending a hand
items.summary: We break down the Citrus Ransomware group's attacks: the attackers' TTPs and tooling, including VLESS traffic tunneling and LLM use, plus their links to Toy Ghouls.

items.title: IT threat evolution in Q3 2026. Non-mobile statistics
items.summary: Key trends and statistics on malware targeting Windows and macOS computers and Internet of Things (IoT) devices in Q3 2026.

items.title: IT threat evolution in Q3 2026. Mobile statistics
items.summary: Q3 2026 mobile threat statistics for Android malware, adware, and unwanted software, plus the most notable malware found during the quarter.
